commandNotices.title: Unavailable: safe author updates
commandNotices.message: `gs update` returns `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` before submission. Safe author updates require a public stale-client precondition (DEP-009); parser help does not enable overwriting resources.

commandNotices.title: Unavailable: Admin UI runtime
commandNotices.message: Admin UI serving is unavailable. It needs a published image and verified authentication, startup and readiness mappings. The reserved serve/config syntax does not establish a working Admin component.

commandNotices.title: Unavailable: Storefront runtime
commandNotices.message: Storefront serving is unavailable. It needs a verified reference runtime, publication reads and trusted target selection. The reserved serve/config syntax does not establish a working Storefront component.

commandNotices.title: Optional OIDC: development evidence
commandNotices.message: The optional Linux OIDC graph uses core profile version 2 and has separate development evidence. Native release host qualification covers the core profile. Running this graph does not add CLI browser/device/OIDC login support.

commandNotices.title: Linux workloads and optional components
commandNotices.message: Workload execution requires a qualified Linux host. `--add admin` and `--add storefront` are unavailable. `--add oidc` is a separately evidenced development graph, not an extension of core host qualification. The core runtime pins GitStore alpha.8.

commandNotices.title: Explicit static-user provider only
commandNotices.message: These session operations require the configured alpha.9 `static-users` v1 contract and matching server. Browser/device/OIDC discovery and arbitrary providers are unavailable (DEP-001).

commandNotices.title: Local logout and remote invalidation differ
commandNotices.message: Default logout removes local OS-store material only. `--remote` requires the configured alpha.9 static-user provider and server confirmation; it is not arbitrary-provider token revocation.

commandNotices.title: Typed watches: restricted kinds and selection
commandNotices.message: Use the explicit alpha.9 contract. Collection watch (DEP-002) and `--id` watches (DEP-018) are unavailable. Streams observe future changes; they do not provide correlated readiness waits or an atomic list/watch snapshot.

commandNotices.title: Creation is limited to mapped kinds
commandNotices.message: Product/Category creation is supported; Namespace/Repository creation requires the explicit alpha.9 contract. Collection/File creation and arbitrary CRDs remain unavailable. Remote `--wait` is unavailable (DEP-004).

commandNotices.title: Deletion is limited to mapped kinds
commandNotices.message: Collection deletion (DEP-002) and File deletion (DEP-007) are unavailable. Accepted deletion starts termination; it does not prove completed cleanup. Remote `--wait` is unavailable (DEP-004).

commandNotices.title: Profile and export limits
commandNotices.message: File ID reads, hydrated YAML and writable `--authoring -o markdown` projections require the explicit alpha.9 contract. Lossy authoring exports and plain Markdown presentation are unavailable. Remote `--wait` is unavailable (DEP-004).

commandNotices.title: Bounded lists and unavailable File listing
commandNotices.message: File listing is unavailable (DEP-007). Each invocation returns one bounded page, not a full multi-page snapshot. Hydrated YAML requires the explicit alpha.9 contract. Remote `--wait` is unavailable (DEP-004).

commandNotices.title: Built-in mappings, not server discovery
commandNotices.message: These commands inspect local versioned core mappings. They do not discover a server, arbitrary CRDs or additional capabilities. Select the profile matching your server explicitly.

commandNotices.title: Submission only
commandNotices.message: Sync submits existing fast-forward history. Transport acceptance does not prove admission or readiness. It does not commit, merge, reset, rebase or force-push. Remote `--wait` is unavailable (DEP-004).

commandNotices.title: Registered local migration only
commandNotices.message: Migration requires a supported Linux deployment, an explicitly registered target and backup acknowledgement. It does not upgrade the pinned alpha.8 data layout to alpha.9 or promise general schema compatibility.

notes: Proposed capability baseline: requires current-head human maintainer approval through Docs release eligibility before merging. See site/release-evidence.json.

Reviewed alpha.6 source 01440a78153ccb9803556e5560307b40dda73a6f against alpha.7 source 8e3f5c18e4141b9baeded53271f1e09625d1eea4: crates/gs/src has no differences and the bundled command reference digest is unchanged. Existing command capability notices remain valid.

Canonical installation examples use alpha.7 published hosted filenames and one shared release.sigstore.jsonl bundle; older alpha.5/alpha.6 diagnostics and per-file verification history stay explicitly historical.
Homebrew requires checking the tap's formula version: it can lag publication while its formula PR is reviewed. Direct APT/DNF/npm instructions select the exact alpha.7 assets.
Native core qualification covers Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora 44 on x86_64 and arm64. macOS is remote/control only.
The managed core runtime pins GitStore alpha.8. Selecting the explicit alpha.9 remote contract does not upgrade local images or establish provider/host qualification.
Remote alpha.9 client paths and optional OIDC retain the source guides' separate controlled/development evidence and qualification caveats.
Admin, Storefront, browser/device/OIDC discovery, safe author updates, correlated remote waits, Collection mutations/watch, and File upload/list remain gated.

Schema 2 records the last reviewed capability baseline independently of generated version/asset prose. Source hashes normalize only marked release blocks; the renderer independently checks every generated block, including root README.md.

Unchanged capability inputs can carry this audit to a later release. Changes to production sources, dependencies, runtime/profile pins, build or qualification inputs require a new reviewed capability baseline; equal parser help alone is insufficient.
